name: flagforge-anti-slop
description: Visual quality gate that rejects generic AI-generated dashboard patterns in FlagForge and forces deliberate recomposition.
---

# FlagForge Anti-Slop

## Prime test
Ask:
"Could this have been generated by asking an AI for a modern dark cybersecurity dashboard?"

If yes, stop and redesign.

## Reject
- endless rounded cards
- card inside card inside card
- every property becoming a pill
- emoji/unicode as primary UI iconography
- neon-green hacker aesthetic
- Matrix rain
- fake terminal backgrounds
- cyberpunk decoration for its own sake
- generic shields/skulls
- random circuit-board wallpaper
- generic 3D security objects
- giant gradient blobs
- glassmorphism everywhere
- excessive glow/shadow
- gradient text/buttons everywhere
- identical card grids across pages
- everything centered
- identical radius on everything
- fade-up on every element
- decorative code with no information value

## Recomposition rule
If a component looks like:
"title + subtitle + four pills + rounded card + shadow + tiny icon"
do not polish it. Recompose it.

Consider:
- open layout
- divider
- typographic hierarchy
- anchored metadata
- framed workspace
- asymmetry

## Card test
Use a card only when the surface expresses a meaningful relationship or boundary.

## Pill test
Use a pill only for compact category/state information where the shape improves scanning.

## Color test
If neon green is being used because "cybersecurity = hacker", reject it.
Return to graphite + forged amber + steel blue-gray with restrained semantic colors.

## Decoration test
For every decoration, ask what it communicates and why it belongs to FlagForge.
No answer => remove.

## Motion test
Keep motion only when it communicates interaction, navigation, feedback, progression, or state.

## Identity test
Mentally hide the logo.
Would the UI still be recognizably FlagForge?
If not, strengthen geometry, typography, SVG language, composition, and competition-specific states.

## Final rule
Do not ask "Does this look modern?"
Ask "Does this look intentionally designed for FlagForge?"
